key_highlights: Grim week wipes $169 billion from the ASX (^AXJO) as recession fears escalate amid sharp market-wide de-risking.
Australian unemployment surges to a five-year high, signalling labor market deterioration and bringing an effective end to RBA rate hikes.
Major department store David Jones faces acute distress with 1,700 redundancies, accelerating market share transfer to Myer (MYR.AX).
Sydney and national housing downturn intensifies following cumulative rate hikes, increasing credit risk for major domestic banks.
AUD/USD depreciates heavily, creating tailwinds for unhedged gold and resources exporters while compounding domestic import inflation.

sectors.trend: Severe retrenchment in household discretionary spending leading to widespread workforce cuts and retail restructuring.
sectors.implications: Elevated downside risk for discretionary retailers; market consolidation benefits competitors like Myer (MYR.AX) picking up displaced sales and suppliers.

sectors.trend: Rising credit risk and margin compression as unemployment climbs, borrowing power shrinks, and residential property values drop.
sectors.implications: Headwinds for the Big Four (CBA.AX, NAB.AX, WBC.AX, ANZ.AX); NAB faces additional reputational drag from payroll underpayment scrutiny.

sectors.trend: Strong capital raising and exploration momentum in gold and critical minerals, supported by a depreciated Australian dollar.
sectors.implications: Favourable cash margin expansion for domestic gold and rare earths producers (NST.AX, EVN.AX, FRS.AX) offsetting broader industrial weakness.

sectors.trend: Suburban commercial strip vacancies widening and residential asset values falling steeply.
sectors.implications: Underperformance across retail and diversified REITs (SCG.AX, DXS.AX, SGP.AX) due to asset write-downs and softening tenant covenant strength.

sectors.trend: Domestic gas market tightness and policy disputes over major infrastructure like Snowy Hydro 2.0.
sectors.implications: High domestic gas realizations bolster upstream operators (WDS.AX, STO.AX, ORG.AX), though energy cost pressures weigh on commercial users.

sectors.trend: Defensive sector positioning preserved alongside long-term dietary shifts driven by GLP-1 weight-loss pharmaceuticals.
sectors.implications: CSL.AX and global healthcare players offer defensive USD-linked revenue streams during domestic economic downturns.

key_themes: RBA tightening cycle ends as surging unemployment pushes Australian economy to the brink of recession
Consumer spending contraction accelerates corporate restructuring and suburban commercial vacancies
AUD weakness provides operational currency hedge for ASX resource and gold exporters
Housing downturn accelerates, elevating credit risks for leveraged households and domestic lenders

risk_assessment.mitigation: Overweight defensive, cash-generative sectors including healthcare and non-discretionary staples; reduce domestic cyclical beta.
Underweight major domestic banks and mortgage-exposed financials; avoid residential property developer stocks.
Hold USD-earning multinationals and natural resources with low domestic input cost exposure.

risk_assessment.risk_factor: Retail and Commercial Real Estate Solvency
risk_assessment.mitigation: Reduce allocations to retail REITs and discretionary consumer stocks facing tenancy and margin compression.

opportunities.rationale: Depreciated AUD and macroeconomic instability drive record local currency margins for gold miners.
Myer is well-positioned to capture customer footfall, vendor relationships, and market share from insolvent David Jones.
Resilient non-cyclical balance sheets and significant earnings tailwinds from the weakening AUD/USD.

defensive_moves.rationale: Surging unemployment and falling home values exacerbate loan delinquency risks and cap credit growth.
Substantial weekly equity sell-off indicates institutional de-risking; downside protection advised.
Surging strip vacancies and department store distress impair rental revenues and asset valuations.

market_outlook.short_term: Cautious and bearish for the ASX 200 (^AXJO) over 1–3 months as earnings downgrades and recession risks are priced in.
market_outlook.long_term: Neutral to constructive over 6–12 months on expected RBA rate cuts providing monetary relief and liquidity support.
key_catalysts: RBA monetary policy statement and official rate cut timing guidance
Monthly labour force data and unemployment rate trajectory
Christmas retail sales data and David Jones liquidation developments
Chinese industrial demand indicators and iron ore benchmark movements
watch_list: Australian unemployment rate breaching further cyclical highs
AUD/USD support levels against the USD
Major bank 90+ day mortgage arrears and impairment charges
Capital raise appetite across small and mid-cap mining juniors
